comment: SYNQED Business territory — the ONLY paths a Business PR may touch (phone-safety lock 3, deny-by-default). Every entry is a directory prefix and MUST end with '/'. Consumed by check-business-isolation.mjs (CI diff gate) and business-isolation.test.ts (import-isolation gate). Business i18n lives inside src/business/ — messages/*.json is in the thin bundle's dependency graph and stays phone-owned. "writers" (⚖ Liam 9/24, R-A2-15 §4) = every write site Business territory may contain, one row per { file, call, symbol } exactly as CP3 (audit-sdk-write-sites.test.ts) prints it; CP3 fails any territory write site with no row. "sharedCores" (PLAN-BUSINESS-LIVE v2.2 §2 S1, W0 PR (1)) = every place Business territory may call one of the phone's shared mutation cores, one row per { module, call, symbol } — only doorFile may import the listed modules, check-shared-cores.mjs fails any site in it with no row, and a "never" name fails even with a row; "class" = core-emits (the core writes its own audit row — valid only for a proven AUDITED_CORES symbol of that module: in its symbols[], not in its unproven[], the set CP7 proves emits on every non-error path) · caller-emits (any other core, e.g. createCustomerWithClient, which leaves the audit row to its caller — the door function emits it itself, so the same symbol needs a trace or receipt row, and an audit call beside the write) · trace (the door calls audit(): fire-and-forget, the sink catches failure — audit.ts:71–84) · receipt (the door awaits auditDurable() and reports its ok — audit.ts:130–142). This file is outside territory, so a row lands in its own non-Business PR before (or with no need of) its code — a row with no site yet is allowed.
